# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (first)
- Strategy tried: diagnosed the 10-task val split directly, then shipped FIVE edit classes in one candidate (in-body auto-correct, dict normalization, arithmetic recompute, enriched returns, policy rules) rather than one timid lever. Every code lever was replayed on the exact failing-trace arguments against the LIVE airline DB and shown gold-exact before shipping — this is the decisive quality gate for a DB-hashed benchmark where you cannot run the eval yourself.
- Key leverage insight: reward = DB × COMMUNICATE, and the dominant zero-score cause is NOT wrong DB logic but (a) the write never executing because an error forces a 2nd confirmation that the user-sim ends with ###STOP###, and (b) a correct DB with the dollar figure never spoken. So the highest-leverage code move is to make the FIRST write succeed (auto-correct amounts/format/baggage in-body) and the highest-leverage comms move is to hand the weak model the exact $ in the return.
- Plateau/stall signal: none yet (iteration 1).
- What to try next: let the gate tell us which levers moved; reserve prose worked-examples for the reasoning clusters (multi-write completeness, multi-reservation split) that code cannot safely encode.

## Iteration cand_0002
- Strategy tried: on a noisy gate (SE=0.1, n=10) where cand_0001's big batch landed within noise (LEDGER row 1, rejected −0.100), switch from "throw everything" to "maximize signal-to-noise": ship only edits that are strictly no-op on correct input (fire-only-on-error code guards) plus a clean bounded new win (cancel-flown guard, task 37) and targeted policy clarifications for the biggest cluster (decoy reservation 17/22). Dropped cand_0001's two widest/refuted edits (dict-return enrichment, prose same-turn anti-STALL).
- Used a read-only diagnosis subagent across all 30 trajectories FIRST — it corrected two intake hypotheses (task 37 = extra forbidden cancel not COMMUNICATE; `'HATHAT'` ids are tool-returned). Diagnosing before editing prevented two wasted levers.
- Every code lever replayed on the exact failing-trace args against the live DB and shown gold-exact + no-op-on-correct before shipping — the decisive quality gate when you can't run the eval yourself.
- Plateau/stall signal: STALL/narrated-without-action remains the one systemic cluster with no safe lever found yet (prose refuted, composite unsafe here). If this iteration is also flat, the next move is a narrowly-scoped safe composite, not another prose rule.
- What to try next: gate-driven — keep the four code guards (strictly safe), and treat the policy prose block as the swing factor to trim if broke={} recurs.

## Iteration cand_0003 (LAST of run, 3/3)
- Strategy tried: build ADDITIVELY on the accepted champion cand_0002 rather than re-batching. Kept all four verified code guards + policy §1–§6 verbatim, and added only strictly-no-op surface: a DB-safe `payment_summary` return key (returns are not hashed) plus three prose decision rules. Rationale: cand_0002 cleared the noisy gate (+0.217) by raising signal-to-noise; the way to not lose that is to not perturb any already-correct decision — a new key and STOP-only rules change no passing DB state.
- Re-interpreted a prior "dropped" lever correctly: cand_0001's dict-return enrichment was dropped in cand_0002 as "low coverage", but its RESULT was broke={}/fixed={} = within-noise, NOT a regression. cand_0001's own RESULT said "the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign." So I did not abandon it — I made it SHARPER (exact copy-ready directive + §4 telling the weak model to prefer the returned figure over its own estimate, with the ×N-passengers worked example that is exactly task 11's failure mode). Meta-lesson: distinguish "within-noise, make it bigger" from "regressed, redesign" when reading RESULT lines — they look similar (both broke={}) but call for opposite moves.
- Plateau/stall signal: the two remaining DB-zero clusters are now cleanly characterised as UN-leverable from the agent side on this split — (a) uncontrollable USER_STOP (simulator ends the episode in the user's confirmation turn), (b) model flight/passenger selection and multi-reservation split (reasoning, not encodable without overfitting). This is the real ceiling of prompt+tools edits on this 10-task val split; further gains need either eval-side (more trials to de-noise) or a benchmark-side fix to the USER_STOP bundling, not another capability edit.
- What to try next run: if the objective ever adds cost/latency, run detect_loop_patterns.py (free) for a bulk-tool opportunity. For reward, the only untried safe lever is a narrowly-scoped confirm+write composite for the unambiguous single-action path — design it so cancel/update stay refusable (cancel-flown guard, basic-economy flight-change) so it cannot defeat the task-37-class guards.
